The project will use **Vite + vanilla JavaScript ES modules + Three.js**, with one selected game and a reusable `shared/` layer.

```text
project/
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── vite.config.js
├── index.html
├── README.md
└── src/
    ├── main.js                    # Application bootstrap
    ├── shared/
    │   ├── core/
    │   │   ├── GameLoop.js        # Fixed simulation step, interpolation
    │   │   ├── InputController.js # Keyboard and Gamepad unified actions
    │   │   ├── ObjectPool.js      # Bounded allocation and reuse
    │   │   └── ResourceScope.js   # Resource ownership and disposal
    │   ├── rendering/
    │   │   ├── RenderPipeline.js  # Renderer, composer, bloom, output
    │   │   └── Procedural.js      # Geometry and Canvas texture helpers
    │   ├── physics/
    │   │   └── Collision.js       # Handwritten collision primitives
    │   ├── vfx/
    │   │   ├── EffectsManager.js  # Effect coordination and priorities
    │   │   ├── CameraShake.js     # Trauma, decay, impact scaling
    │   │   ├── ParticleManager.js # Pooled instances; hard cap of 500
    │   │   ├── HitStop.js         # Bounded simulation time dilation
    │   │   ├── MotionTrails.js    # Pooled trail segments
    │   │   ├── ShockwaveRings.js  # Pooled expanding emissive rings
    │   │   └── FloatingText.js    # Pooled world-anchored score labels
    │   ├── audio/
    │   │   └── AudioSystem.js     # Procedural Web Audio synthesis
    │   └── ui/
    │       ├── Overlay.js        # Reusable overlay lifecycle
    │       └── glass.css         # Glass panels and neon accents
    └── [GameName]/
        ├── plan.md               # Detailed plan for the selected game
        ├── Game.js               # Lifecycle and state transitions
        ├── config.js             # Rules, tuning, pool capacities
        ├── World.js              # Procedural scene and PBR materials
        ├── Gameplay.js           # Mechanics and collision resolution
        ├── Entities.js           # Pooled game-specific entities
        ├── HUD.js                # Game-specific interface
        └── game.css              # Game-specific presentation
```

`[GameName]` will become the **exact selected collection name**. Its module breakdown will be finalized during planning.

Dependencies flow from `main.js` to the selected game, then into `shared/`. Shared modules never import game-specific code. All visual and audio assets are generated in code; mesh materials use `MeshStandardMaterial`. The rendering pipeline includes `EffectComposer` and tuned `UnrealBloomPass`.

- **Anti-Lazy Directive:** Every approved file and function will be fully implemented, with consistent imports and a playable loop reaching a win or loss state.
- **Strict Memory Management:** Explicit resource ownership, bounded pools, instancing where applicable, and disposal of geometries, materials, textures, render targets, and other owned resources.
- **Sequential Output Protocol:** Initialization now; exhaustive planning after `Begin [Game Name]`; implementation only after `Plan approved`. If output truncates, `continue` resumes exactly where it stopped.

Which game are we starting with? Reply **`Begin [Game Name]`**.
